title: Agent That Adapts to New Tasks
subtitle: Design an operations agent that learns new tasks on its own, adapting in the cheapest reversible place first and sending every self-change through the same gate as a human change.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: What adapt means and what changes the design
practice_prompts.hint: Name the five rungs and the discovery questions whose answers move the design.

practice_prompts.label: Two loops, one gate and the registry
practice_prompts.hint: Trace a known and a novel request, then a candidate from trace to live.

practice_prompts.label: Gate numbers and what they prove
practice_prompts.hint: State 5, 200, 4 and 3 points, and the sample-size limit of a 200-attempt shadow.

practice_prompts.label: Autonomy bounds, failures and cost
practice_prompts.hint: Separate what the agent may change from what only a human may, then answer the cost pivot.

rubric: Defines five rungs from context to weights and starts from the cheap, reversible end.
Detects novelty with more than one signal and runs unknown tasks in a tighter fallback mode.
Requires an external outcome signal for Reflexion and skill promotion, never self-grading.
Leads memory design with a four-gate write policy, typed facts and supersession.
Gates every candidate on held-out, paired, per-stratum evaluation with a 3-point floor, then shadow and auto-demotion.
Explains that 200 shadow attempts prove 'not much worse', not a 5-point gain.
Keeps permissions, budgets, irreversible actions and re-promotion with humans.
Funds fine-tuning only for format at volume, missing vocabulary or a cost or latency ceiling.
Answers the cost pivot through candidate dedupe, staged suites and learning spend per promotion.

editorial_review.evidence: Built a 104-row inventory from the 62 captured sections (27 Interview Guide parts, 35 Answer Template sections, intro), splitting rich sections such as the sizing, gate and weights parts into separate mechanism rows. The guide and template repeat the ladder, architecture, failures, MVP and 60-minute plan; these are merged into one walkthrough step each, with every template-only detail (Kubernetes/serverless example, 0.43/0.75 threshold, max retries 2, six audit questions, contradictory-memory and infinite-retry rows, 1,000-case variant) kept and named. I rechecked all sizing products and worked the sample-size formula at p = 0.8 into the text. Source gaps handled: the fast-learning trade-off had only a figure, explained as the demotion net; the prompt-optimisation section's admitted lack of optimiser sources is kept. First-person interview phrasing outside spoken examples was recast. The brief opens on the ops agent and the unreviewed-regression constraint, defines skill, rung, gate, shadow and stratum, and gives a short Orion trace before the task, since the five-rung vocabulary is otherwise unfamiliar. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): 'five controls' with four named → five listed, the fifth (permission changes always need a human) taken from the guide's own autonomy table; Orion diagrams one step off their text → placed beside the steps they depict and the reader-facing note about the misplacement removed.
